findings.title: State projection uses only the last entry writer and loses retained or derived source restrictions
static_facts: scoped_state builds last_writers by replacing each field's writer with the operation matching the latest mutation event.
It skips a field when that writer is None; native Evolution events without a C1 operation are therefore not source-filtered here.
For a mapped writer it checks only that operation's entry, not the field's retained values or the original ThinkSession/context ancestry.
origins has no engine.subject-state case. EntryPermission therefore does not independently recover these state-field origins.
The current W04 TEST provider sets update_subject_state=False and supplies no proposed_mutations. The existing related-memory regression does not exercise the multi-writer field scenario.
findings.impact_inferred_from_source: A restricted value can survive in a list field after B appends an unrelated allowed value, while the whole field is thereafter treated as B-origin. Native or indirect state changes can also lose entry provenance. Such a field can enter B's composed context despite withdrawal of A-to-B transfer.
required_counterexamples: Through the original C1/Thinking/Action/Evolution path, write an identifiable A-only marker to a legal list-valued state field; revoke A-to-B transfer; append B-local content to the same field; ask B about the topic. Check the exact final context and any emitted content, retaining the original persisted state/history.
Exercise a native ThinkSession or indirect B update that derives a state value from A, followed by withdrawal, including reopen.
Assert both exclusion of the A marker and continued availability of B-local material; blanket state exclusion is not a valid repair.
findings.repair_constraint: Use original state mutation semantics, Event/ThinkSession and existing provenance. Preserve state/history, current permissions, and the sole authoritative store. Do not merely label an entire accumulated field by its last writer.

findings.title: Entry authorization precedes later observation callbacks even inside the final dispatch guard
static_facts: _current calls entry.delivery_current at line 109, then connection_guard and self.observe at line 117, followed by attachment/action and lifecycle checks.
The trailing require_action checks the device attachment and ability; it does not re-evaluate entry read_from, binding fingerprint or user-level contact_pauses.
DeviceOperationService.execute invokes the original ExecutionService.current inside the port's final guard, so that final guard repeats this same ordering.
SimulatedDevice.execute calls guard, compares the device state hash, then records the effect; its state comparison does not validate the separate entry configuration.
findings.impact_inferred_from_source: If entry transfer permission, recipient binding, or contact-pause state changes during the last device observation while the device view/attachment remains unchanged, the final guard has no subsequent entry-specific authorization check before the simulated send.
required_counterexamples: Arm a controlled hook only for the final port-held guard. During its device observation, withdraw A-to-B transfer or change the B binding while preserving the device state hash. The send must have zero effects and zero cost.
In the same final-observation window, activate the user-level contact pause. Verify no B/C send and preserve independent lawful internal cognition.
Retain unchanged-permission success controls; verify a later legitimate new request works after reauthorization without silently rebinding an old sealed context or replaying UNKNOWN effects.
findings.repair_constraint: Close the original synchronous dispatch boundary after the remaining callbacks. Preserve P17, the existing request/receipt identity and device transaction; do not claim distributed or arbitrary production revocation guarantees.
